title: Ranking of Kings
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Prince Bojji, born deaf and tiny to a family of giants, is mocked as unfit to rule. He befriends Kage, the last survivor of a slaughtered assassin clan, who understands him. After King Bosse dies, the court passes the throne to Bojji's half-brother Daida, and Bojji sets out on a journey while a plot involving a magic mirror and a demon unfolds at home.
life_message: True strength is kindness and perseverance, and even wrongdoers can be understood and forgiven.

content.note: Clan massacre, assassination attempts, betrayal and lost limbs (Wikipedia; ANN; AniList Assassins, Amputation tags).
Demon bargain, underworld monsters and a possessed king (Wikipedia; AniList Demons tag).
Bojji ridiculed for deafness and size (Wikipedia; AniList Bullying, Disability tags).
Betrayal and attempted murder shown as wrong and later regretted (Wikipedia: Domas).

dominant: Kindness as strength; disability and worth; forgiveness of villains; critique of power-worship

Order vs freedom.evidence: Royal court, oaths and loyalty to the king structure life.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Gods, demons and the ranking frame the world.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Bojji's growth and acceptance of difference, amid danger.

folkways.japan: Absolute loyalty to a lord (Domas, Hokuro) echoes Japanese retainer ideals, while Bojji's gentle perseverance reflects valued endurance (gaman), noted as context.

delivery.evidence: ANN (anime) says it argues for 'empathy and forgiveness' and is 'asking a lot of its audience' with forgiving villains.

personified.ideology: Becoming strongest is worth any price
Only the physically capable should rule

delivery.note: Power-worship is embodied by sympathetic, remorseful characters rather than cartoon villains; the forgiveness message is earnest.

winners_losers: Bojji's kindness wins allies and the throne; power-seekers such as Bosse and Miranjo are shown as damaged and are understood, even forgiven.
